brief: AI didn't kill my job — it made me realize I hated my job. 6 reframes for technical founders.

slots.subtitle: Artificial intelligence exposed the cage I had mistaken for a career. Here are six keys out.
slots.preview1: Why competence without ownership is just expensive burnout
slots.preview2: The three questions that separate operators from founders
slots.preview3: How to trade salary for sovereignty without going broke

slots.title: You are not
slots.subtitle: The identity trap that keeps technical founders renting out their brains.
slots.insight1Body: Senior Engineer is a rental agreement, not a life sentence.
slots.insight2Body: Being good at something you hate is a very expensive prison.
slots.insight3Body: Equity in your own work beats salary in someone else's empire.
slots.pullQuote: I was paid well to ignore the fact that I had no control.

slots.title: Efficiency without
slots.subtitle: Optimizing a path you didn't choose is just faster misery.
slots.insight1Body: Shipping features for a product you don't own is athleticism with no finish line.
slots.insight2Body: Automation without ownership accelerates someone else's vision, not yours.
slots.insight3Body: The founder's edge is choosing what to build, not how fast to build it.
slots.pullQuote: AI made my old job easier, which made it harder to justify staying.

slots.title: Safety is a
slots.subtitle: A single paycheck is not security; it is concentration risk in human form.
slots.insight1Body: An employer is a customer who owns your entire calendar and ego.
slots.insight2Body: Product, design, and distribution matter more than any single codebase.
slots.insight3Body: Three micro-products teach you more than five years of sprint planning.
slots.pullQuote: I traded the illusion of safety for the reality of optionality.

slots.title: Ship the
slots.subtitle: The market does not ask for your resume; it asks for your product.
slots.insight1Body: A computer science diploma validates the past, not your next product.
slots.insight2Body: A thousand followers who trust you outrank any Fortune 500 logo.
slots.insight3Body: Working code and revenue speak louder than polished LinkedIn headlines.
slots.pullQuote: Nobody asked where I studied after I showed them what I shipped.

slots.title: Build in
slots.subtitle: Every hour spent consuming is an hour spent funding someone else's leverage.
slots.insight1Body: Writing about your builds creates compound interest in attention and trust.
slots.insight2Body: Explaining your code in public establishes authority faster than any promotion.
slots.insight3Body: A newsletter with five thousand readers is a more durable asset than stock options.
slots.pullQuote: I stopped reading the news and started writing the documentation for my own life.

slots.title: Start before
slots.subtitle: The perfect moment is a procrastination device sold to employees by other employees.
slots.insight1Body: You do not find your product idea; you stumble on it while building.
slots.insight2Body: Two focused hours a day on your own work beats eight hours of meetings.
slots.insight3Body: The price of a failed product is tuition; the price of inaction is your life.
slots.pullQuote: I was never ready to leave. I just ran out of reasons to stay.

slots.ctaBody: These six reframes are a permission slip to stop optimizing a life you didn't choose. Build yours instead.
